blocks.text: The standard deviation measures how dispersed data are around the mean. A low standard deviation means the data cluster tightly around the mean; a high one means they are spread out; a value close to zero means the points are very close to the mean. In biology it is used to assess variability in measurements such as plant growth rates or enzyme concentrations.

blocks.alt: Two bell-shaped curves with dashed lines at the mean. (a) A wide, low orange curve with a long arrow marked 1 SD: high standard deviation. (b) A narrow, tall blue curve with a short arrow marked 1 SD: low standard deviation.
blocks.caption: High and low standard deviation (original diagram after the book's curves).
blocks.long_description: Standard deviation measures how dispersed data are around the mean. When values are spread out the curve is wide and low and the standard deviation is high; when values cluster tightly around the mean the curve is narrow and tall and the standard deviation is low. A standard deviation close to zero means the data points are very close to the mean.

blocks.text: Formula: standard deviation (sigma) = square root of [sum of (xi - mu) squared / N], where xi is each data point, mu the mean and N the number of data points. Steps: find the mean; subtract it from each value; square each deviation; average the squares (this is the variance); take the square root.

blocks.caption: Standard deviation of nine plant heights

blocks.text: Variance = 784 / 9 = 87.11, and standard deviation = square root of 87.11 = 9.33 cm.
